ety.text: Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰeh₂-der. Ancient Greek χαῦνος (khaûnos) Ancient Greek χάος (kháos)der. Dutch gasbor. English gas Borrowed from Dutch gas, coined by chemist Jan Baptist van Helmont in Ortus Medicinae. Derived from Ancient Greek χάος (kháos, “chasm, void, empty space”); perhaps also inspired by geest (“breath, vapour, spirit”). Doublet of chaos. First attested in 1648.
Clipping of gasoline. Slang forms popularized on TikTok by Gen Z.
Compare the slang usage of "a gas", above.

senses.d: Matter in an intermediate state between liquid and plasma that can be contained only if it is fully surrounded by a solid (or in a bubble of liquid, or held together by gravitational pull); it can condense into a liquid, or can (rarely) become a solid directly by deposition.
ex: A lot of gas had escaped from the cylinder.

senses.d: A flammable gaseous hydrocarbon or hydrocarbon mixture used as a fuel, e.g. for cooking, heating, electricity generation or as a fuel in internal combustion engines in vehicles, especially natural gas.
ex: Gas-fired power stations have largely replaced coal-burning ones.

senses.d: Poison gas.
ex: The artillery fired gas shells into the enemy trenches.

senses.d: A chemical element or compound in such a state.
ex: The atmosphere is made up of a number of different gases.

senses.d: A hob on a gas cooker.
ex: She turned the gas on, put the potatoes on, then lit the oven.

senses.d: Methane or other waste gases trapped in one's belly as a result of the digestive process; flatus.
ex: My tummy hurts so bad – I have gas.
But anyone with that many large brown birds aroost in his cranium and that much gas in his bottom was clearly not a well person.

senses.d: The supply of natural gas, as a utility.
A humorous or entertaining event, person, or thing.
ex: Two more girls came in, one in bright pink stretch pants and the other in purple. “Man this place is a gas,” said pink.
No it really doesn't matter at all / Life's a gas / I hope it's going to last

senses.d: Frothy or boastful talk; chatter.
ex: Bang, little boy, stop with the gas / Little T, man he chats up his ass

senses.d: A fastball.
ex: The closer threw him nothing but gas.

senses.d: To attack or kill with poison gas.
ex: The Nazis gassed millions of Jews during the Holocaust.
He never fully recovered after he was gassed on the Western Front.

senses.d: To use poison gas in (a volume or area) to attack or kill someone or something.
To talk in a boastful or vapid way; to chatter.
ex: "Well don't keep on gassing about it," said Digory.

senses.d: To impose upon by talking boastfully.
To emit gas.
ex: The battery cell was gassing.

senses.d: To impregnate with gas.
ex: to gas lime with chlorine in the manufacture of bleaching powder

senses.d: To singe, as in a gas flame, so as to remove loose fibers.
ex: to gas thread

senses.d: Gasoline, a light derivative of petroleum used as fuel.
An internal virtual currency used in Ethereum to pay for certain operations, such as blockchain transactions.
ex: gas fee
The average “gas fee” – transaction cost – of an Ethereum transaction is between US$85 and US $156, according to crypto.com data.

senses.d: Marijuana, typically of high quality.
To increase the fuel flow to a vehicle's engine in order to accelerate it.
ex: The cops are coming. Gas it!

senses.d: To fill (a vehicle's fuel tank) with fuel.
Of high quality.
ex: This food is gas.

senses.d: Comical, zany; fun, amusing.
ex: Mary's new boyfriend is a gas man.
It was gas when the bird flew into the classroom.

From Old French, from Latin essentia. Sense 2 very likely from Latin edō (“eat”), in the sense of 'what is eaten, fuel'. Many forms of the latter are indistinguishable from the former, and so the confusion with essence is very understandable.

senses.d: A flammable liquid consisting of a mixture of refined petroleum hydrocarbons, mainly used as a motor fuel; petrol.
ex: You can't put gasoline in this car. This car takes diesel fuel.
So you punched out a window for ventilation. Was that before or after you noticed you were standing in a lake of gasoline?

senses.d: Any specific kind of this fuel.
ex: He was trying to invent a cleaner-burning gasoline.
The refinery produces a wide range of gasolines.

senses.d: Marijuana, especially very potent or of high quality.
An alcoholic beverage made of vodka and energy drink.
Made from or using gasoline.
